overview: This bill expands burial benefits from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). Currently, when the VA provides an urn or commemorative plaque for a veteran whose ashes are not buried, the family must take it instead of a headstone or grave marker; the bill would let families receive both, for veterans who died on or after January 5, 2021. It also removes a cutoff date so that eligible family members of veterans who died before November 11, 1998, can also qualify for certain VA memorial headstones and markers. It also extends, to May 31, 2033, an existing limit on VA pension payments to certain veterans living in nursing homes paid for by Medicaid, which helps offset the bill's costs. As of October 17, 2025, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say families should not have to choose between an urn and a headstone to honor a veteran, and that an old cutoff date should not keep some families from receiving memorials.
against: Critics say the new benefits are paid for by extending a cap on pension payments to low-income veterans in Medicaid nursing homes, shifting costs onto one group of veterans to fund benefits for another.
